result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_articulation_points()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find articulation points (cut nodes) in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L24977-L25020){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_articulation_points() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Articulation points](/assets/graphs/get-articulation-points.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two triangles joined by the path C, D, E. The nodes C, D, and E are in the accent color: removing any one of them splits the graph. The card lists the articulation points C, D, E." width="100%"} An articulation point is a node whose removal disconnects the graph or increases the number of connected components. Uses Tarjan's DFS-based algorithm. Only defined for undirected graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of node IDs that are articulation points. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If graph is directed. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a path graph `1-2-3-4-5`, every node except the two endpoints is an articulation point: removing any of them splits the path into two disconnected pieces: ::: {#868aa7f2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(5) cut_node_ids = graph.get_articulation_points() # Returns 3 (the three interior nodes) len(cut_node_ids) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: ## Common Use Cases {.doc-common-use-cases} - network vulnerability analysis: Critical infrastructure nodes - social networks: Key influencers whose removal fragments communities - communication networks: Single points of failure
